Meeting header: 2026-02-07 16:00 PST | Duration: 42 min
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Sam Patel (Nimbus CTO); Maya Lopez (Nimbus ML Eng); Jordan Kim (Nimbus Platform)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll go for about 40 minutes today, demo + parity mapping discussion. Priya is gonna run through the console and API examples. Sam: sounds good thanks. Maya: hi all.
[00:22] Priya: quick agenda: 1) show API parity (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood) 2) console walkthrough Optimize settings 3) embeddings + rerank 4) security and deployment options 5) next steps. is that what you had in mind? Sam: yep that's great.
[01:05] Priya: ok starting with model names — on OpenAI you might be using gpt-4o or gpt-3.5, Anthropic would be claude-2 or 3, Together might be together-j1, the mapping in Redwood is straightforward, we expose a model catalog and have recommended equivalents e.g. gpt-4o -> redwood-instruct-4o, claude-2 -> redwood-chat-2, together-j1 -> redwood-j1-compat. note these are our product names and performance profiles. Maya: are those drop-in compatible at the API call level? do we need to change prompt formats? Priya: mostly no — we map the core parameters: model, temperature, max_tokens, stop sequences, top_p. function calling is a bit different, we expose tool-calls via function/tool calling API similar to OpenAI's functions but with small differences in schema. we'll show code in a sec.
[03:10] Priya: (screen share) here's a simple python snippet we use: client.generate(... model='redwood-chat-2', messages=..., temperature=0.2, max_tokens=512) — same idea as openai.ChatCompletion. for function calls we accept a 'tools' list with json schemas; Redwood returns a 'tool_call' event in streaming. sam: streaming is important for us, latencies matter for our UI. how does streaming compare? Priya: streaming is supported, we stream tokens and tool events. our median first-byte latency on hosted for 8k context is ~120-160ms in our Seattle region in our benchmarks, your mileage may vary. Jordan: we run in eu-west for compliance, can you guarantee region routing? Alex: yes we have region routing policies and Dedicated/Private for regional compliance.
[06:00] Maya: embeddings — we currently use OpenAI embeddings ada-002 and anthopic (typo) embedding models, will embeddings be compatible for semantic search? Priya: embedding vector dims may differ slightly, but we provide recommended mapping and a migration path: reindexing pipeline or on-the-fly dual query approach. our redwood-embed-384/1024 map to common dims; most customers reindex for best recall. Sam: cost for reindexing is our main concern. Alex: we can run a pilot with selective reindexing and measure recall delta.
[08:20] Priya: Console: here's the per-route perf dashboard, cost breakdown by token, token-level traces, and Optimize suggestions. Optimize will recommend batching, kv cache TTLs, and quantized model variants. Maya: can Optimize suggest when to move to dedciated or quantized family to reduce cost? Priya: yes it suggests model/quantization and predicted cost savings.
[10:45] Jordan: security — we need SOC2, SAML/SSO, audit logs, HSM/KMS for key management, and VPC peering for Private deployments. also data residency EU. Alex: Redwood is SOC2, we support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs. Private includes VPC/on-prem with KMS integration, HSM via partner integrations, and audit log forwarding. sam: ok can we get the security docs? Alex: we'll send SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and our private-deployment checklist.
[13:30] Maya: what about rate limits and throttling — our app is bursty, we have spikes during peak traffic. Priya: you can use Dedicated reserved pools to absorb bursts; also there's autoscale and burst capacity config. we can set per-customer quotas and token-rate limits. for hosted, we suggest reserve or dedicated if you need consistent p99 latency.
[15:12] Sam: can we keep same behaviour for stop tokens and streaming partials? some of our pipelines rely on stop sequence heuristics. Priya: yes stop sequences are supported; we also support structured output options and response schemas which helps with parsing. slight differences in escape handling sometimes appear — it's usually minor.
[16:40] Priya: demo time — I'll paste an example of an assistant with function calling: messages -> tool schema -> single call -> Redwood returns a tool_call event then tool_result. note transcription: sometimes our tool call payload naming is slightly different (e.g., 'tool_name' vs 'name' in some legacy schemas) we keep compatibility shims. Maya: good to know.
[19:05] Priya: embeddings example: call embed(texts=[...], model='redwood-embed-1024') returns vectors. we have a wrapper library to convert OpenAI embeddings payloads to Redwood's, so minimal code changes. Sam: is there a migration lib we can use? Priya: yes we'll share a migration helper repo and sample scripts.
[21:00] Jordan: about benchmarks — can you run our dataset against redwood and openai side-by-side? we want latency and cost per 1M tokens and quality metrics (accuracy on intent classification). Alex: yes SE-led benchmark, we can run on Hosted or Dedicated depending on need. estimated 3-5 days to run and analyze for a small corpus. Maya: do you support token-level breakdowns? Priya: yes console + API metrics include token-level cost and the Optimize tool produces suggestions.
[23:10] Sam: any gotchas with Together models or Anthropic guardrails? Priya: Anthropic's safety system behaves differently; we recommend A/B tests for customer-facing prompts. Together sometimes has different tokenization edge cases — again we recommend spot-checking and setting guardrails.
[25:30] Maya: can we keep audit proof testing and have evals attached to rollouts? Priya: yes rollouts can be canary or A/B and we have eval hooks to run prompt set tests and quality regression alerts.
[27:00] Alex: pricing — hosted per-token, dedicated monthly commits. we'll send ballpark pricing for your current usage; AE note: Nimbus currently on 1.2B tokens/month (Sam confirmed earlier). Sam: right, roughly 1.2B tokens, mix of chat and embeddings. Alex: ok will send dedicated sizing and example cost savings with quantization and batching.
[29:18] Maya: network & infra — if we do Private, do we need egress rules? Jordan: they ask about NAT and peering. Alex: yes private requires peering and network config; we'll share network checklist. Jordan: how long to set up Private trial? Alex: typically 4-8 weeks depending on approvals and infra.
[31:05] Priya: demo end, quick Q&A: Maya: can we keep prompt templates and SDK wrappers? Priya: yes our SDK supports same patterns; we have migration guides for python/js and wrappers to shim old calls.
[33:22] Sam: ok next steps recap? Alex: we'll send parity mapping doc, security kit, pricing and Dedicated options. Priya will run benchmark after you share sample prompts. we'll schedule POC kickoff week of 2/23. Sam: sounds good.
[34:10] Alex: any objections or blockers now? Sam: main blocker is cost and reindexing effort. Alex: we can do a limited reindex pilot focused on top 10% queries to bound cost. Maya: and we need EU data residency — ensure Private/Dedicated in eu-west. Alex: noted.
[36:00] Jordan: one more question: function calling streaming in the client — is there WebSocket or SSE support? Priya: SSE for streaming is supported and websockets for longer-lived sessions via our SDK. Jordan: ok great.
[37:30] Sam: can you send a simple contract or MOU for a short pilot? Alex: yes I'll send a pilot MOU and pricing example.
[38:15] Alex: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with docs and action items. meeting adjourned.
